newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Remgro says no Malbak decision yet.
newsitem.headline: Remgro says no Malbak decision yet.

text.p: The Rembrandt Group (Remgro), which is rumoured to be keen to buy Malbak Ltd in which it already holds a stake, said on Thursday that it had not made any decisions regarding its investment in the company.
"We've not decided what to do regarding our investment or the future of Malbak," Remgro managing director Thys Visser told said.
Asked to comment on market talk that Remgro was keen to buy Malbak and merge their packaging interests, Visser told Reuters:
"I really can't comment on that type of speculation. Many things could happen to Malbak."
Malbak cautioned shareholders it was in talks that might have an effect on the share price.
Visser said Remgro currently held 18 percent of Malbak.

South Africa's Business Times newspaper said on Sunday that it was "common knowledge in the market" that Remgro was eyeing Malbak, which recently underwent a rigorous unbundling exercise which has left it as a focused packaging company.
The unbundling saw Malbak sell off its unlisted assets and distribute the shares in its underlying listed subsidiaries to shareholders.
"Up to now we've tidied (our Malbak stake) up by exchanging the underlying shares that we received for further Malbak shares basically to consolidate the position," Visser said.
The newspaper said Remgro would merge Malbak with its packaging operations which are held largely through a 30 percent stake in Printpak and a 17 percent stake in Lenco.
Malbak's primary assets since the unbundling are a 68 percent stake in Kohler Ltd and a 64 percent interest in UK-listed MY Holdings Plc.
By 1330 GMT Malbak shares had jumped 32 cents to 710 cents on rumours of a possible takeover. Shares in Lenco were 85 cents better at 700 cents but Remgro was unchanged at 46.00 rand.
"If there are further developments we'll make further announcements," Visser added.
